heroHeadline: Suicide Bombing Kills 21+ at Kohat Police Lines Mosque as Pakistan Reports 17 Militants Killed in KP, Balochistan IBOs
heroSubtitle: September 18, 2026 is Day 9,112 since the US launched Operation Enduring Freedom and Day 206 of Pakistan's Operation Ghazab lil-Haq. A vehicle-borne IED and gunmen assault struck a mosque inside the Kohat Police Lines compound in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa during Friday prayers, killing at least 21 people — 15 police officers and 6 civilians, per Dawn, with Al Jazeera citing local officials putting the toll as high as 27 — and wounding more than 100. Ittehadul Mujahideen, a Hafiz Gul Bahadur-linked TTP faction formed in April 2025, claimed responsibility; security forces killed six of roughly seven attackers during the clearance operation. The same day, Pakistan's ISPR reported 7 Fitna al-Hindustan militants killed in intelligence-based operations in Panjgur and Kachhi, Balochistan, under 'Radd-ul-Fitna 3'. The bombing caps a bloody week: ISPR says security forces killed 10 militants in North Waziristan and Hangu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa between September 15-17, while a September 17 IED attack on a security convoy killed 6 soldiers. On September 14, security forces killed 9 Fitna al-Hindustan militants, including commander Naqeeb, in Mastung and Pishin, Balochistan. Separately, Taliban Justice Minister Abdul Hakim Sharei detained Afghanistan's Supreme Shia Council head Mohammad Ali Akhlaqi and four members in a Ministry of Justice 'private prison' in Kabul on September 13, extending a crackdown on Shia institutions that began with the seizure of the Khatam al-Nabieen seminary. No formal ceasefire or new Urumqi round has been confirmed.
